audit_status: draft; source-checked seeds, not an exhaustive historical open-problem certification
scope: Total languages over finite binary strings. AC0, ACC0, TC0 and NC1 are nonuniform; NC is logspace-uniform. Promise-class containments are restricted to total languages, never conversely.

sources.title: Complexity Limitations on Quantum Computation
sources.notes: Fortnow and Rogers. Author full text: https://lance.fortnow.com/papers/files/quantum.pdf. Explicit total-language BQP definition.

sources.title: Quantum Arthur-Merlin Games
sources.locator: Abstract and the strong QMA amplification theorem / containment in PP
sources.notes: Marriott and Watrous. Primary theorem gives QMA contained in PP; restricting yes/no promise to a partition gives the language containment.

sources.title: Quantum Computational Complexity
sources.notes: Watrous's author survey. Used for machine/circuit definitions and direct simulation derivations, not as the primary source for QMA contained in PP.

sources.title: Gap-Definable Counting Classes
sources.locator: Abstract: Few contained in SPP; GapP closure; definitions of counting classes
sources.notes: Fenner, Fortnow and Kurtz. Author PDF https://cse.sc.edu/~fenner/papers/gaps.pdf has poor extracted text; readable definitions and inclusion chain also checked in q-ffkl02.

sources.title: An Oracle Builder's Toolkit
sources.locator: Section 2.1, Definition 2.3, printed pp. 5–6; Section 6.1, Definition 6.2 and Lemma 6.3
sources.notes: Fenner, Fortnow, Kurtz and Li. PDF dated 2002-11-11; expanded version of 1993 conference paper. Gives readable counting definitions, FewP–SPP–LWPP–WPP–C=P–PP chain and WPP contained in AWPP.

sources.title: Small Bounded-Error Computations and Completeness
sources.notes: Böhler, Glaßer and Meister. Primary authors' paper states MA contained in SBP contained in AM intersect BPPpath and BPPpath contained in PP; language-level gap definitions are explicit.

sources.title: Honest-Verifier Statistical Zero-Knowledge Equals General Statistical Zero-Knowledge
sources.locator: Section 1, especially printed pp. 1–2: HVSZK contained in AM intersect coAM; HVSZK closed under complement; theorem HVSZK=SZK
sources.notes: Goldreich, Sahai and Vadhan. For AM upper bound authors credit Fortnow and Aiello–Håstad; for complement closure Okamoto and Sahai–Vadhan. Total-language restrictions inherit both conclusions.

sources.title: Can Statistical Zero Knowledge be Made Non-Interactive? or On the Relationship of SZK and NISZK
sources.locator: Theorems 1.5–1.6; explicit warning immediately after Theorem 1.5
sources.notes: Goldreich, Sahai and Vadhan. SZK=BPP iff NISZK=BPP here is explicitly about promise problems. Do not import it as an implication about total-language classes without an additional argument. NISZK is outside the final roster.

sources.title: BPP and the Polynomial Hierarchy
sources.notes: Lautemann's primary publication proves BPP contained in Sigma2P; complement closure also gives Pi2P.

sources.title: In Search of an Easy Witness: Exponential Time vs. Probabilistic Polynomial Time
sources.locator: Main equivalence NEXP contained in P/poly iff NEXP=MA; full journal manuscript Section 4.1
sources.notes: Impagliazzo, Kabanets and Wigderson; JCSS 65(4), 672–694, 2002; preliminary CCC 2001. Full theorem checked at https://www.math.tau.ac.il/~amnon/Classes/2017-BPP/Lectures/IKW02.pdf (abstract and Section 4.1).

sources.title: Algebrization: A New Barrier in Complexity Theory
sources.locator: Theorem 3.5 and paragraph immediately following, printed p. 12; Corollary 3.15; Section 3.5
sources.notes: Aaronson and Wigderson. Taking trivial oracles gives PP contained in P/poly implies P^#P contained in MA. Restricting to PP yields the roster rule; Toda also yields PH contained in MA.

sources.title: Separating QMA from QCMA with a Classical Oracle
sources.notes: Bostanci, Haferkamp, Nirkhe and Zhandry. Published before the benchmark cutoff. This is an oracle separation and is deliberately NOT a QMA-versus-QCMA baseline fact.

sources.title: Non-Uniform ACC Circuit Lower Bounds
sources.notes: Williams. Journal of the ACM, 2014, DOI 10.1145/2559903; preliminary result 2011. Theorem 1.1 strengthens NEXP to NTIME[2^n]. Source ID is stable despite the bibliographic correction.

sources.title: Derandomizing Polynomial Identity Tests Means Proving Circuit Lower Bounds
sources.locator: Authors' abstract, first and second paragraphs
sources.notes: Kabanets and Impagliazzo. The consequence of BPP=P is a DISJUNCTION involving arithmetic permanent lower bounds, not the unconditional Boolean statement NEXP not contained in P/poly.

sources.title: A Complete Problem for Statistical Zero Knowledge
sources.notes: Primary source for the Statistical Difference characterization used by the optional operational SZK definition. The characterization equivalence is not proved in this repository.

rules.justification: IKW gives NEXP=MA; MA contained in NEXP is already known.
Theorem 3.5 with trivial oracles gives P^#P contained in MA. PP and PH are contained in P^#P (the latter by Toda, explicitly used in Section 3.4).
The reverse direction of the IKW equivalence. MA is unconditionally contained in NEXP, so the premise gives NEXP=MA.

complement_pairs.justification: From a 0/1 GapP gap g, use 1−g.
Replace gap g by f(0^|x|)−g; the length-dependent normalizer is unchanged.
Replace gap g by f(x)−g; the FP normalizer is unchanged.
Replace approximating gap g by f−g to exchange the near-zero and near-one intervals.
If membership means integer GapP gap g>0, then 1−2g>0 holds exactly on nonmembers.
Replace GapP gap g by g+1 to exchange odd and even parity.
Flip the output bit, exchanging bounded-error acceptance and rejection.
HVSZK is closed under complement and equals SZK; Section 1 credits Okamoto and Sahai–Vadhan for the complement theorem.
coMA is defined as the set of complements of MA languages.
coAM is defined as the set of complements of AM languages.
coQMA is defined as the set of complements of QMA languages; this is not a claim QMA=coQMA.

notes: The search checked cited statements and selected 2025–2026 updates. It did not prove absence of all pre-cutoff results. Unreached pairs must be unclassified until curator certification, rather than automatically called open.
No unrelativized strict separation between BQP and BPP, NP and BQP, or QMA and QCMA is seeded. Oracle results do not resolve those ordered pairs.

A promise-class inclusion restricts to a total-language inclusion. A separation witnessed only by a promise problem need not yield a total-language separation. The benchmark currently misses that second type of result.
BPP=P for total languages does not by itself permit replacing a verifier's promise-BPP problem by a P machine. In particular this file does not encode BPP=P implies MA=NP or QCMA=NP.
The q-gsv99 equivalence between NISZK=BPP and SZK=BPP is explicitly for promise classes and is not encoded for the total-language roster.
Neither SBP nor CeqP is assigned self-complement closure. Their complement closure is not known here; this is not a proven nonclosure.
parityP contained in PP is not a known seed. Exact parity and a threshold are different counting conditions.
Do not encode BPP=P implies NEXP not contained in Ppoly: Kabanets–Impagliazzo gives a disjunction with an arithmetic circuit lower bound, which this pair-only rule language cannot express.

The nonuniform circuit convention is essential. Nonuniform AC0 already contains undecidable length languages and must not be included in P or L. Its known reverse separations from all decidable roster classes should be provided by the classical baseline.

All source years are document/publication years, not the search engine's sometimes misleading crawl or republication date. Later revisions require a pinned historical-version audit before eligibility is frozen.
